discussion.title: Packages take a long time to become visible to conda search after upload
discussion.body:
I regularly see that packages that get uploaded to https://anaconda.org/conda-forge take ~1 hour or more (as timed by the _Uploaded_ timestamp on the `/files` page for that package) to become visible with `conda search`. Is there an way to more regularly update the package list (repodata?) for a channel to have packages become usable with a lower latency?

My current example is `osx-64/python-lalburst-1.5.9-py310h93fb10b_2.tar.bz2` which was _Uploaded_ '1 hour and 6 minutes ago' by `cf-staging`, but isn't available from `conda search`

```console
$ date && conda search python-lalburst=1.5.9=py310h93fb10b_2
Fri Dec 10 07:19:40 PST 2021
Loading channels: done
No match found for: python-lalburst==1.5.9=py310h93fb10b_2. Search: *python-lalburst*==1.5.9=py310h93fb10b_2

PackagesNotFoundError: The following packages are not available from current channels:

  - python-lalburst==1.5.9=py310h93fb10b_2

Current channels:

  - https://conda.anaconda.org/conda-forge/osx-64
  - https://conda.anaconda.org/conda-forge/noarch

To search for alternate channels that may provide the conda package you're
looking for, navigate to

    https://anaconda.org

and use the search bar at the top of the page.
```

Is there anything that I ('the user') can do to speed things up?

nodes.body: Update: this package became available around about 0729 PST (December 10), so approximately 75 minutes after being uploaded.

Packages that are uploaded to `conda-forge` are mirrored to a CDN. As it takes some time to do the mirroring, they don't show up immediately.

That said, it is typically closer to ~30mins. 75mins does sound a bit long. @chenghlee do you have any thoughts here?

Digging through the logs on the sync worker, since 2021-09, each CDN sync run now takes ~47 minutes; about 60% of that time (~28 min) is spent running `conda index`.

These numbers seem to be mostly independent of the number of packages being synced, so there's definitely something a little to a lot weird going on. I've opened a ticket with Anaconda's Infrastructure team to take a look at what's going on, though given the time of year, we may not have a real answer until Q1 of next year.

Another current data point (2026-08-28):

- Package: conda-forge/liquilens-evidence 0.15.0, build pyhc364b38_0
- Feedstock build succeeded: https://github.com/conda-forge/liquilens-evidence-feedstock/actions/runs/33152963342
- Anaconda upload time: 07:51:46 UTC
- More than one hour later, the package API and the explicit conda-forge/label/main artifact return 200, and the artifact SHA-256 is 5995bb7250dc34dc94715825e82038a1a48441d68950ccfa2f6a7d708f0f7877.
- The ordinary conda-forge/noarch artifact URL still returns 404, while current_repodata.json and channeldata.json do not contain liquilens-evidence.
- A fresh micromamba solve using only -c conda-forge cannot resolve liquilens-evidence=0.15.0. The same public artifact installs successfully from the explicit label/main channel and both package entry points pass smoke tests.
- Anaconda status currently reports all systems operational.

Package page: https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/liquilens-evidence
Feedstock: https://github.com/conda-forge/liquilens-evidence-feedstock

Is a delay beyond one hour currently expected for default-channel replication/indexing, or is there a specific service or queue maintainers should inspect?
